case.title: Silver Blaze
case.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
case.summary: Silver Blaze, favourite for the Wessex Cup, has vanished from the King's Pyland stables on Dartmoor, and his trainer John Straker has been found dead on the moor with his skull crushed, a knife in one hand and a stranger's cravat in the other. The stable-lad on guard was drugged with opium in his supper. The police have arrested Fitzroy Simpson, a bookmaker who was seen at the stables that evening trying to bribe his way to a tip. Holmes is asked to find the horse and the murderer.
case.solution_summary: Straker, deep in debt from a secret second household kept under the name William Derbyshire, planned to lame his own horse so that it would lose. Curried mutton was served that night, and Straker put opium in the stable-lad's portion, where the curry hid its taste. At one in the morning he went down to the stable (the dog knew him and kept quiet), led Silver Blaze to a hollow out of sight, took off his coat, and struck a match to light his candle and nick the horse's tendon with a cataract knife. The startled horse kicked him in the head and killed him; falling, he cut his own thigh. The horse bolted towards Mapleton, where Silas Brown found it at dawn and hid it, disguising its white markings, until Holmes made him produce it for the race.
case.teaser: A Sherlock Holmes story by Arthur Conan Doyle, first published in 1892.

scenes.title: Breakfast at Baker Street
scenes.summary: Holmes announces he must go to Dartmoor; Watson joins him and brings his field-glass.
source: I am afraid, Watson, that I shall have to go

scenes.title: The train: the facts of the case
scenes.summary: Holmes states the facts from the papers and telegrams, and the police theory. Watson suggests the knife wound was self-inflicted.
source: We are going well

scenes.title: Tavistock and the drive with Gregory
scenes.summary: Gregory gives the latest: Simpson's answers, the gypsies, Mapleton searched. Holmes falls silent and arrives 'day-dreaming'.
source: It was evening before we reached the little town of Tavistock

scenes.title: Straker's villa: the pockets and Mrs. Straker
scenes.summary: Holmes examines what Straker had in his pockets, including a cataract knife and a milliner's bill to 'William Derbyshire'. He tests Mrs. Straker about a dress.
source: Excuse me,

scenes.title: The hollow
scenes.summary: The overcoat was placed, not blown. Holmes finds a buried wax vesta, compares boots, pockets the horseshoe, and tells Ross to keep the horse entered.
source: A short walk across the moor took us to the hollow

scenes.title: Across the moor to Mapleton
scenes.summary: Holmes reasons the horse must be at Mapleton, finds its tracks, then a man's tracks beside them looping towards King's Pyland and back. He confronts Silas Brown, who capitulates.
source: It’s this way, Watson

scenes.title: The walk back
scenes.summary: Holmes tells Watson how he broke Brown: square-toed boots, Brown always first up, the horse recognised by its white forehead. He announces their return to London.
source: A more perfect compound of the bully, coward, and sneak

scenes.title: Departure: the photograph, the sheep, the dog
scenes.summary: Holmes asks for Straker's photograph, puts a question to the maid, asks about the sheep, and points Gregory to the dog in the night-time.
source: Not a word more could I draw from him

scenes.title: The Wessex Cup
scenes.summary: A horse in Ross's colours with no white hair wins. Holmes reveals it is Silver Blaze in disguise — and that the horse is Straker's killer.
source: Four days later Holmes and I were again in the train

scenes.title: The explanation on the train home
scenes.summary: Holmes explains the curry, the dog, the knife, the bill, the sheep, the milliner, and the death in the hollow.
source: We had the corner of a Pullman car to ourselves that evening

inconsistencies.summary: The race is 'next Tuesday', but the narration puts it 'four days later' than the Thursday of the investigation — a Monday. The time windows stay abstract (w.race_eve, w.race_day) so neither reading is baked in.
source: preventing Silver Blaze from being there at the fall of the flag next Tuesday
I have every hope, however, that your horse will start upon Tuesday

inconsistencies.summary: The race is called the Wessex Cup throughout, but the race card names it the Wessex Plate.
source: the race for the Wessex Cup
Wessex Plate.

inconsistencies.summary: Holmes tells Ross the horse 'bolted, and was cared for by one of your neighbours', though in s07 he says Brown deliberately hid it. The first is Holmes softening it for Ross, under the 'amnesty' he grants.
source: Ah, it bolted, and was cared for by one of your neighbours.
We must have an amnesty in that direction

inconsistencies.summary: The room where the pockets are examined is the 'sitting-room' / 'front room'; Ross and Gregory later wait in the 'parlour'. They may be the same room; kept as two places because the text never says so.
source: We all filed into the front room
The Colonel and the Inspector were awaiting us in the parlour.

notes: Holmes keeps almost all his reasoning back until s10; a game hands that reasoning to the player.
The one investigative action whose result is never told is Holmes's question to the maid (a.question_maid). A game adaptation must invent it or drop it.
External note (not from this text): Doyle later admitted his ignorance of racing rules — a disguised horse could never have been allowed to run (Memories and Adventures, 1924).
r.gypsies_avoid_trouble is a period stereotype voiced by Holmes; flagged for any adaptation.
Glosses marked editorial are written for this game, not taken from the story; they say what an 1892 reader would have known.
